letterNameAssessment.en: 26 American English letter names, including zee, are coherent with the configured en-US course.
letterNameAssessment.es: 27 letters include Ñ. Ye and uve doble are accepted standard names; do not treat regional alternatives such as i griega/doble u as inherently wrong.
letterNameAssessment.fr: 26 letter names are plausible native spellings for the spoken names. No new text correction justified.
letterNameAssessment.de: 26 basic names plus umlaut names and Eszett are coherent. The names are not being presented as every possible phoneme value.
letterNameAssessment.it: The 21 traditional Italian letters are correctly ordered; the summary already says standard letters. Loanword letters J/K/W/X/Y are an expansion opportunity, not evidence that the taught 21-letter sequence is wrong.
letterNameAssessment.pt: 26 Brazilian Portuguese names include K/W/Y. Dáblio and ípsilon are valid names; no speculative spelling replacement justified.

pictureTeachingAssessment.taskMeaning: Active Western picture-alphabet tasks explicitly ask which character completes an example word and state that the image depicts the word, not a letter’s meaning.
pictureTeachingAssessment.importantDistinction: French H in thé, Spanish H in coche, German I in Bein, and similar internal/digraph examples are spelling-gap tasks. They must not be described as first-sound or universal letter-pronunciation examples.
pictureTeachingAssessment.pixelCoverageLimitation: All 156 text mappings were read and validated, but only the six images listed above were newly visually inspected in this supplement. Do not claim all underlying pixels or recorded pronunciations were certified.

sources.supports: German has 26 basic alphabet letters, plus Ä/Ö/Ü and ß; letters and sounds are distinct.
Uve and uve doble are established letter names.
Italian has 21 traditional letters and five non-native letters used in loanwords.
Dáblio/dâblio names the letter W; valid variants should not be replaced speculatively.
